condition.label: Chronic primary low-back pain
condition.distinctions: Chronic primary/nonspecific low-back pain is separate from nerve-root pain, specific pathology, stenosis and postoperative states. Mechanical-nociceptive trial subgroup is narrower than the inventory diagnosis.

scope.population: Recurrent mechanical/nociceptive-dominant low-back pain; Mechanical nociceptive-dominant low-back pain over three months; primarily ages 25–60; nerve-root compression/acute disc herniation and specific pathology excluded
scope.stage: Varies by source; acute/recent versus chronic and symptom irritability are explicitly retained. Unknown stage remains unknown.
scope.operativeStatus: Nonsurgical evidence predominates; no postoperative protocol approved or inferred.
scope.exclusions: Source-specific exclusions are applicability boundaries, not diagnosis-wide contraindications. Coexisting conditions and independently selected joint limits retain precedence.
scope.uncertainty:
- Ordinary training: preserve activity, tailor tolerable starting demand and progression. Do not encode diagnosis-wide bans on flexion, extension, rotation, axial loading, squats or deadlifts; retrieved studies do not justify them. LBP-P2's neutral deadlift technique is protocol-specific, not proof of harm from all spinal motion.
- Supportive candidates: general progressive strengthening, motor-control work, aerobic exercise; select exact executions only after catalog comparison. No novel identity required solely because an exercise is described as “core.” Stretching remains mobility, not strength-set credit.
- Unresolved: universally safe load/ROM/pain threshold, acute flare algorithms, safe unsupervised high-load dose, subgroup effects, and older-adult transfer. Specific pathology, postoperative restrictions and radicular symptoms cannot inherit this record.
- Currentness search found a 2025 Cochrane overview (DOI 10.1002/14651858.CD014691.pub2; PMC11945228) and a 2026 JAMA clinical review; they were located but not fully extracted. They do not replace direct execution-level evidence. No claim of exhaustive current coverage.

sources.outcomes: Hayden et al., 2021 Cochrane review. DOI 10.1002/14651858.CD009790.pub2, PMID 34580864, PMC8477273. Abstract and publisher conclusions inspected; not all underlying trials. 249 RCTs, 24,486 participants, chronic nonspecific LBP >12 weeks. Earliest follow-up: exercise versus no treatment/usual care/placebo reduced pain 15.2/100 (95% CI 12.2–18.3), functional limitation 6.8/100 (5.3–8.3); functional difference below review's clinical-importance threshold. Heterogeneity and trial bias matter. Adverse reporting insufficient to establish comprehensive safety; reported events mostly minor muscle pain. No evidence here for a blanket spinal flexion, rotation, squat or lifting ban.

sources.population: Mechanical nociceptive-dominant low-back pain over three months; primarily ages 25–60; nerve-root compression/acute disc herniation and specific pathology excluded
sources.comparator: High-load deadlift versus low-load motor control
sources.outcomes: Michaelson et al., 2016 same-cohort RCT follow-up. DOI 10.2340/16501977-2091, journal full text PDF. FT. 35/group; mechanical LBP >3 months; 8-week intervention, 2-,12-,24-month outcomes. No significant between-group pain/disability/QoL differences; no untreated control. Deadlift progression was supervised and contingent on pain before/during/after; no 1RM testing. Two high-load participants reported adverse effects, one withdrew; none reported in low-load arm. Selected population and close technique/progression supervision limit unsupervised generalization. Supports individualized progression and a lower-load alternative; not a rule that all patients must avoid deadlifts or remain neutral in every daily movement.
sources.uncertainty: No untreated control; close supervision and selected phenotype limit app transfer

sources.limitations: No untreated control; close supervision and selected phenotype limit app transfer Trial exclusions delimit studied applicability; they do not establish general contraindications.

protocol.execution: Barbell deadlift with abdominal bracing/breath hold and monitored neutral lumbar alignment; low-load arm individualized lumbar control in supine/sitting/quadruped/standing
protocol.dose: 12 treatments over eight weeks; deadlift began 10 kg including bar, sets/repetitions/load individually adjusted, no 1RM test
protocol.frequency: Twice weekly first month, once weekly thereafter; low-load arm 1–3 daily home exercises
protocol.progression: Increase repetitions/sets/load only when pain had not increased before/during/after; PT and participant decide; intervening symptom increases considered
protocol.stoppingRules: not reported as numeric cutoff; pain increase altered progression, not an approved app rule
